title: Investigate and fix misbilling when rate limits and KV-cache hits interact with speculative decoding
creator: Avery Chen
description: Summary: Multiple customer reports and internal audits show overstated token debits when a request is both rate-limited (throttled/backpressured) and benefits from KV-cache prefix hits while the model runtime performs speculative decoding. Symptoms: (1) final token tally sometimes includes provisional speculative tokens that should have been rolled back on rate-limited aborts, (2) prefix KV-cache credits are double-counted when speculative frames are merged with resumed frames after a backpressure event, and (3) rate-limiter telemetry shows 'allocated' credits not matching ledger finalization. Hypothesis: provisional speculative tokens are being recorded in the session ledger before the rate-limiter or stream-finalization path confirms commitment. When a request is throttled or requeued, the provisional credits are not being reconciled against the KV-cache prefix cache hits, resulting in persistent overcounts. Scope: affects streaming text generation paths with speculative decoding enabled (runtime path: mux -> speculative worker -> kvcache -> rate-limiter) across hosted and dedicated deployments. Reproducible with our internal harness using intermittent artificial latency injected into the rate-limiter to force preemption and retry across the worker pool.
acceptance_criteria: No customer-facing token overcharges in rerun of the repro harness across 1M simulated requests (pass/fail),
Session ledger only finalizes committed tokens after stream-finalization hooks regardless of speculative decoding outcomes
Rate-limiter shows zero leaked allocated credits in the grafana query (query link in links) for the reproducer run
Unit tests covering: provisional-credit lifecycle, kvcache hit reconciliation, and rate-limiter preemption path are present and green
Integration e2e test added to the metering CI that simulates midstream preemption + resume with kvcache hits
technical_notes: Root causes identified during initial debugging: (1) provisional speculative tokens are appended to the session's in-memory ledger immediately by speculative worker thread instead of emitting a tentative delta that must be ACK'd by the finalizer; (2) kvcache grants prefix advantage which reduces perceived token consumption but the refund path assumes a strict linear sequence (no preemption), leading to double-count when speculative frames are later merged with resumed outputs; (3) rate-limiter tracks 'allocated' counters per session but the final commit path subtracts only confirmed tokens. Proposed fix: adopt a two-phase crediting model for speculative outputs: emit 'provisional' credits to a separate provisional ledger namespace keyed by session+attempt-id, don't increment global allocated counters until the finalizer transitions provisional->committed. When preemption occurs, the finalizer will reconcile kvcache adjustments and move the minimal committed amount. Implementation plan: add provisional ledger table in the metering service (in-memory with persistent checkpointing), plumb attempt-id through speculative worker and resume code paths, update rate-limiter to accept provisional reservations and only apply to global allocations on final commit, and add a kvcache reconciliation pass that deduplicates prefix-derived savings across provisional and resumed frames. Tradeoffs: small increase in memory footprint and complexity in ledger state machine. Performance impact should be negligible because provisional entries expire on commit/abort and reconciliation runs are cheap O(n) per session where n is number of speculative frames (normally small).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch with flag ENABLE_PROVISIONAL_CREDITS off by default. 2) Run in internal canary traffic (10% of test cluster) with metering debug logs enabled for 48h. 3) If canary stable, enable for dedicated customers only for 72h. 4) Full rollout in runtime-1.21 pending metric thresholds. Rollback: flip flag off and run reconcile job to move any lingering provisional entries back to previous model (scripts provided).
test_plan: Unit: provisional ledger lifecycle (create, commit, abort, ttl-expiry)
Unit: kvcache reconciliation dedupe across speculative+resumed frames
Integration: harness that injects 100k intermittent preemptions, validate no net overcharge (compare ledger snapshot to expected)
Integration: rate-limiter stress test to ensure no deadlocks when provisional reservations are held for short durations
E2E: staged rollout checks with internal billing dashboard and alerting configured
